direction.premise: Cyndaquil's tiredness appears as sputtering flames caused by incomplete combustion.
direction.audiencePromise: See how Cyndaquil's back turns fatigue into a visible flame signal.
direction.openLoop: Why do Cyndaquil's flames sputter instead of simply growing weaker?
direction.payoff: Its back works like a visible tiredness meter: vigorous when angry, sputtering when tired.
direction.engagementQuestion: Better detail: a flame meter or a weird science quirk?

voice.instructions: Sound like a knowledgeable fan sharing a surprising detail. Keep the pace quick, warm, and clear. Punch the words tired, sputter, and incomplete combustion. Pause briefly before the final either-or question.

scenes.headline: TIRED FIRE SPUTTERS
scenes.narration: When Cyndaquil is tired, its flames sputter.
scenes.caption: TIREDNESS HAS A FLAME SIGNAL

scenes.headline: ANGER MAKES FIRE VIGOROUS
scenes.narration: When Cyndaquil is angry, flames from its back burn vigorously.
scenes.caption: ANGRY = VIGOROUS FLAMES

scenes.headline: THE PATTERN BREAKS
scenes.narration: But tiredness changes the flame pattern into fitful, uneven bursts.
scenes.caption: FITFUL • UNEVEN • SPUTTERING

scenes.headline: NOT JUST WEAK FIRE
scenes.narration: The Pokédex calls those sputters incomplete combustion, not simply weak fire.
scenes.caption: INCOMPLETE COMBUSTION

scenes.headline: A FLAME-POWER METER
scenes.narration: So its back becomes a visible tiredness meter: steady or sputtering.
scenes.caption: STEADY → SPUTTERING

scenes.headline: METER OR SCIENCE QUIRK?
scenes.narration: Better detail: a flame meter or a weird science quirk?
scenes.caption: FLAME METER OR SCIENCE QUIRK?
